images.caption: View of Mocha (Yemen). Part of a series of prints related to the Austrian-Ottoman war (1683–1699), and which included Mediterranean and Red Sea views as well as views of biblical places. Published c. 1690 by Antwerp-based Jacques Peeters. The etchings were done by Gaspar Bouttats, Lucas Vorstermans and Coenraad Lauwers. This particular specimen as well as the information come from the online map gallery of map seller PAULUS SWAEN.

images.filename: South Arabian - A Lion and a Leopard Attacking Animals - Walters 2171.jpg
images.caption: On the left side of this relief, an Asiatic lion attacks a gazelle, while a rabbit tries to jump away from the gazelle's forelegs. On the right, an Arabian leopard jumps down from rocks onto the back of an ibex; a small rodent flees the hoofs of the ibex. Birds in the branches of acacia trees observe the two scenes. The frieze was broken in two during the civil war in Yemen in 1962, and the longer right section was discolored by fire.

images.caption: "Faiz , the health worker, was explaining to me how they give plumpynut to mothers to take home to cure their children. However about a third of the mothers do not come back with their children for more to complete the three week programme. They 'default'. He explained that sometimes they feed their child with all of the plumpy nut rather than in small regular doses. This can lead to the child refusing the plumpynut. Other times they forget to wash their hands leading to diarrhoea. Or they complement the plumpy nut with other foodstuffs they should avoid. All of which can mak their situation worse. I looked at the package and saw that it was written in english, and there were no instructions. The mothers are generally illiterate and arabic speakers. It suddenly occurred to me we should put pictures on the packet explaining how to use it, just like Potnoodles!" (Original description from Flickr); foto album title on Flickr: "Razeh district in Sadah"
